title: Print the rules version at the top of the itemator job log

mr_description:
Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-ai-hackathon/transcend-october-2026/39194174/showcase/-/work_items/22

## What
`itemator.ci.main` now prints `itemator rules vN` (N = `RULES_VERSION` of the rules that run) as the first line of the `itemator` job log, so nobody has to open `itemator.json`. It is printed right after argument parsing, so it also appears when the job fails.

title: Show a progress bar while the registry lookup runs in the job
mr_title: Draft: Draft: Show a progress bar while the registry lookup runs
mr_description:
## What
Shows a progress bar in the `itemator` job log while the registry lookup runs. Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-ai-hackathon/transcend-october-2026/39194174/showcase/-/work_items/25

- `itemator/registry.py`: `look_up` takes an optional `progress(done, total)` callback (called before the first lookup and after each package; `total` is the packages that will be visited, so it respects `PER_EXTRA`). New `progress_bar` draws `Looking up packages on the registries [#####---] 5/10` on stderr, overwriting one line and ending it when done.
- `itemator/ci.py`: passes `progress` through `main` -> `run` -> `facts` -> `look_up`. Only `main` (the job) turns the bar on, so library callers and tests are silent by default.
- Standard library only. stdout (card lines and the JSON log block) is unchanged. A broken bar or stream never fails a lookup.

## Verification
- `python3.12 tools/hardcode_audit.py`: 8 passed, 0 failed.
- **Unverified: the pytest suite.** pytest is not installed in this environment and could not be installed (no network), so `python3.12 -m pytest tests` was not run. I added tests to `tests/test_registry.py` (callback sequence, broken callback, bar drawing, bar on stderr not stdout) and checked that file compiles, but they have not been run.
- Instead I ran a standalone script that exercises `look_up` progress calls (7 packages, cap of 5, non-dependency extras), a raising callback, `progress_bar` output, and `facts(progress=...)`; it passed.
- Not seen in a real CI log; the `\r` overwrite is not rendered by every log viewer, but the final line is always complete.

## Beyond the issue
Nothing.

title: Make eval/registry_check.py skip packages it already looked up
mr_title: Draft: Draft: Skip packages eval/registry_check.py already looked up
mr_description:
Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-ai-hackathon/transcend-october-2026/39194174/showcase/-/work_items/27

## What changed
`eval/registry_check.py`, pass 1: a package (same ecosystem, name and pinned version) that was already looked up in the run is not looked up again; the earlier record is reused for the repeat PR. The summary gets a new `repeat_lookups_skipped` count.

## How I checked
- `python3.12 -m py_compile eval/registry_check.py`: OK.
- A synthetic run (same package `foo` in two PRs, `bar` in a third, fake network) made pass 1 skip exactly 1 repeat (`repeat_lookups_skipped: 1`).
- **Not verified:** the real replay. `eval/cache/` is not in the checkout, and the script refuses to run again because `results/registry_facts_devABC.json` exists. I did not regenerate any file under `results/`.
- **Not run:** the test suite. `pytest` is not installed here. No tests cover this script.

## Caveat on the request count
The script's `Polite` fetcher already keeps every answer by (method, url, body) and never sends a request twice. So the number of requests actually sent is the same before and after. In my synthetic run, 2 network calls were made both before and after the change. What this change drops is the repeat lookups themselves: building the request, re-parsing, and a second `Run`. The `repeat_lookups_skipped` field makes them visible. If you wanted fewer network requests than the script already sends, that cannot be reached by this change.

## Beyond the issue
Nothing.

title: Validate .itemator.toml against a published schema
mr_title: Draft: Validate .itemator.toml against a published JSON Schema
mr_description:
Closes https://gitlab.com/gitlab-ai-hackathon/transcend-october-2026/39194174/showcase/-/work_items/28

## What
- New `itemator/policy.schema.json`: a JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) describing `.itemator.toml` (tables, keys, types, quietable kinds, at most 20 patterns of 1 to 200 characters, no control characters).
- `itemator/policy.py` now validates the parsed file against that schema instead of the hand-written checks. The Python standard library has no JSON Schema validator, so a small walker (`_violation`) handles the few keywords the file uses; `_reason` turns the first violation into the same sentences the card shows today.
- The schema sits in `itemator/` on purpose: the CI job exports only that folder from the target branch, so the schema comes from the target branch with the checker.
- `docs/setup.md`: one sentence linking the schema.

## Verification
- **`pytest` could not be installed here (no package index through the proxy), so the real `pytest` run is UNVERIFIED.**
- Fallback: I ran every test in `tests/test_policy.py` (127 of them, including the git-backed end-to-end ones and the parametrized schema cases) with a small stand-in runner that supplies `tmp_path`, `monkeypatch`, `repo` and the autouse fixtures. Result: 127 passed, 0 failed with this change (125 on the unchanged code, plus my 2 new tests). I did not run the other test files.
- Old and new `parse()` compared on 69 inputs (every parametrized case plus extras, and each rule kind): one difference, on a file with two problems at once (`[ignore] kinds = ["nope"]` plus an unknown table `[other]`). The old code named the unknown table first; the new one names the first problem in file order. The file is ignored whole either way; only the reason text differs.
- Mutation check: 43 of 43 mutants of the policy checks and the schema file were killed by that runner (the repo's `eval/mutate_ci.py` itself was not run). `python tools/hardcode_audit.py --only 1 4` passes.

## Beyond the issue
- `eval/mutate_ci.py`: 12 mutant anchors pointed at policy.py lines this change replaces, so I re-anchored them on the new code and added 9 mutants for the schema file. Without this, the script's anchor assertion fails.
- `tests/test_policy.py`: two tests added (schema file matches the checker's constants and `extras.KINDS`; unreadable schema gives a reason). No test deleted or weakened.
- No dependency, CI, or config change.
